'''Genevieve M. Gates''' is an Australian mycologist, ecologist, and taxonomist who is particularly focused on the fungal diversity of [[Tasmania]].

==Work and encouragement of citizen science==
Gates started to publish articles on the macrofungi of Tasmania in 2002 with her long-time collaborator David Ratkowsky,<ref name="Agaricales">{{cite journal |last1=Ratkowsky |first1=D.A. |last2=Gates |first2=G.M. |date=2002 |title=A preliminary census of the macrofungi of Mount Wellington, Tasmania- the Agaricales. |url=https://eprints.utas.edu.au/13511/ |journal=Papers and Proceedings of the Royal Society of Tasmania |volume=136 |pages=89–100 |doi=10.26749/rstpp.136.89 |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref> and finished her PhD in 2009.<ref name=thesis /> In 2014 Gates and Ratkowsky then went on to publish ''A Field Guide to Tasmanian Fungi,'' which at the time was the only in-print work on fungi of the island,<ref name=Campbell>{{cite journal |last1=Campbell |first1=Maxwell |date=2022 |title=Natural History Medallion: Dr Genevieve Gates. |journal=The Victorian Naturalist |volume=140 |issue=2 |pages=55–57}}</ref> and was also a co-author in the laminated field booklet ''FungiFlip: A pictorial guide to Tasmanian fungi''.<ref name=THRoW /> She is a coauthor of ''The Entolomataceae of Tasmania,''<ref>Noordeloos, M and Gates, G.M. ''The Entolomataceae of Tasmania''. Springer, 2012</ref> a major study of the genus ''Entoloma'' in Tasmania.

She is an honorary associate at the [[University of Tasmania]], and volunteers at the Herbarium of the [[Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery]].<ref name=UTAS>{{cite web
	| url = https://www.utas.edu.au/natural-sciences/people/biological-sciences
	| title = People: Biological Sciences
	| website = Discover our expertise
	| publisher = University of Tasmania
	| access-date=12 January 2024
    | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230201113724/https://www.utas.edu.au/natural-sciences/people/biological-sciences?result_1044714_result_page=3
    | archive-date= 1 February 2023
}}</ref><ref name=TMAG>{{cite web
	| url = https://www.tmag.tas.gov.au/collections_and_research/tasmanian_herbarium/tasmanian_herbarium_collection
	| title = Collection at the Tasmanian Herbarium
	| website = Tasmanian Herbarium
	| publisher = Tasmanian Museum and Art Gallery
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
}}</ref> Gates is also called upon to provide advice to medical professionals, when a patient is suspected of ingesting poisonous fungi.<ref name=Campbell />

In her efforts to encourage greater public interest in fungi, Gates established and was involved in the management of multiple special interest [[Facebook]] groups. These included creating the Tasmanian Fungi Facebook page in 2014, and the Field Naturalists of Tasmania Facebook page in 2015.<ref name=THRoW /> Gates also regularly leads excursions to look for fungi, aimed at interested amateurs, and gives lectures and talks.<ref name=Campbell />

==Botanical legacy==
Gates has named over 70 species of fungi,<ref name=THRoW /> including:
*''[[Entoloma albidocoeruleum]]'' G.M.Gates & Noordel.<ref name=Noordel>{{cite journal |last1=Gates |first1=Genevieve M. | last2=Noordeloos |first2=Machiel |date=2007 |title=Preliminary studies in the genus Entoloma in Tasmania -I. |url=https://www.ingentaconnect.com/contentone/nhn/pimj/2007/00000019/00000002/art00001  |journal=Persoonia |volume=19 |issue=2 |pages=157–226 |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
*''[[Entoloma asprellopsis]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2>{{cite journal |last2=Gates |first2=Genevieve M. | last1=Noordeloos |first1=Machiel |date=2009 |title=Preliminary studies in the genus Entoloma in Tasmania -II. |url=https://sciencepress.mnhn.fr/sites/default/files/articles/pdf/cryptogamie-mycologie2009v30f2a1.pdf |journal=Cryptogamie, Mycologie |volume=30 |issue=2 |pages=107–140 |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
*''[[Entoloma austroprunicolor]]'' G.M.Gates & Noordel.<ref name=Noordel />
*''[[Entoloma cystidiosum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma griseosquamulosum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma mathinnae]]'' G.M.Gates, B.M.Horton & Noordel.<ref name="Gates 2009">{{cite journal |vauthors=Gates GM, Horton BM, Noordeloos ME |title=A new ''Entoloma'' (Basidiomycetes, Agaricales) from Tasmania |journal=Mycotaxon |year=2009 |volume=107 |pages=175–9 |url=http://www.entoloma.nl/pdf/175gates8-186.pdf |doi=10.5248/107.175 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100215163007/http://www.entoloma.nl/pdf/175gates8-186.pdf |archivedate=2010-02-15 }}</ref>
*''[[Entoloma melanophtalmum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma natalis-domini]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma psilocyboides]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma strigosum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma tenuicystidiatum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma totialbum]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma transmutans]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
*''[[Entoloma violascens]]'' G.M.Gates and Noordel.<ref name=Noordel2 />
She also collected the type specimen of ''[[Thaxterogaster austrovaginatus]]''.<ref name="Thaxterogaster">{{Cite journal |last=Gasparini |first=B. |date=2007-03-01 |title=Genus Cortinarius, subgenus Phlegmacium in Tasmania |journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany |volume=45 |issue=1 |pages=155–236 |doi=10.1080/00288250709509711 |s2cid=84810334 |issn=0028-825X|doi-access=free |bibcode=2007NZJB...45..155G }}</ref>
{{Botanist|inline=yes|G.M.Gates}}

The specimens collected by Gates in Tasmania are held in herbarium collections around the world.This includes over 2,000 specimens held by the Tasmanian Herbarium,<ref name=tasavh>{{cite web
	| url = https://avh.ala.org.au/occurrences/search?q=collector_text%3A%22Gates%2C%20G.M.%22&disableAllQualityFilters=true&qc=data_hub_uid%3Adh9&fq=collection_uid%3A%22co60%22
	| title = Occurrence records 
	| website = Australasian Virtual Herbarium
	| publisher = Atlas of Living Australia
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
}}</ref> over 4,000 specimens held by the [[National Herbarium of Victoria]], [[Royal Botanic Gardens Victoria]].<ref name=vicavh>{{cite web
	| url = https://avh.ala.org.au/occurrences/search?q=collector_text%3A%22Gates%2C%20G.M.%22&disableAllQualityFilters=true&qc=data_hub_uid%3Adh9&fq=data_resource_uid%3A%22dr376%22
	| title = Occurrence records 
	| website = Australasian Virtual Herbarium
	| publisher = Atlas of Living Australia
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
}}</ref> Outside of Australia, a smaller number are held by the [[Tartu University]] Herbarium, and elsewhere.<ref name=Tartu>{{cite web
	| url = https://elurikkus.ee/generic-hub/occurrences/search?q=Genevieve%20Gates&sort=first_loaded_date&dir=desc#records
	| title = Occurrence records 
	| website = eElurikkus
	| publisher = University of Tartu Natural History Museum and Botanical Garden
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
}}</ref>

==Honours, and awards==
Gates has the following species named after her:
* ''Lactarius genevieveae'' D. Stubbe & Verbeken (now ''Lactifluus genevieveae'')<ref name=THRoW />
* ''Allotrechispora gatesiae'' L.W. Zhou, S.L. Liu & T.W. May<ref name=Zhou>{{cite journal |last1=Liu |first1=S.L. | last2=He |first2=S.H. |last3=Wang | first3=X.W. | first4=T.W. | last4=May |last5=He | first5=G. |last6=Chen| first6=S.L. | last7=Zhou | first7=L.W. |date=2022 |title=Trechisporales emended with a segregation of Sistotremastrales ord. nov. (Basidiomycota). |url=https://www.mycosphere.org/pdf/MYCOSPHERE_13_1_11-1.pdf |doi=10.5943/mycosphere/13/1/11 |journal=Mycosphere |volume=13 |issue=1 |pages=862–954 |access-date=12 January 2024}}</ref>
* ''Fomitiporia gatesiae'' Y.C. Dai & F. Wu [as '''gatesii''<nowiki/>']<ref name=THRoW />
* ''Entoloma gatesianum'' Karstedt & Capelari<ref name=Karstedt>{{cite journal |last1=Karstedt |first1=F. | last2=Bergemann |first2=S.E. |last3=Gates | first3=G. | first4=D. | last4=Ratkowsky |last5=Cunha | first5=K.M. |last6=Capelari| first6=M. | date=2024 |title=Species of Entoloma (Entolomataceae) with cuboidal basidiospores from Brazil. |url=https://phytotaxa.mapress.com/pt/article/view/phytotaxa.654.1.1 |doi=10.11646/PHYTOTAXA.654.1.1 |journal=Phytotaxa |volume=654 |issue=1 |pages=1-76 |access-date=13 September 2024|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
* ''Hydnellum gatesiae'' J.K. Douch, L.J. Vaughan & T.W. May<ref name=Douch>{{cite journal |last1=Douch |first1=J.K. | last2=Vaughan |first2=L.J. |last3=Cooper | first3=J.A. | first4=G.D. | last4=Holmes |last5=Robinson | first5=R. |last6=Stefani| first6=F. | last7=Idnurm | first7=A. | last8=May | first8=T.W. | date=2024 |title=Taxonomic revision of fleshy species of Hydnellum, Neosarcodon, and Sarcodon (Thelephorales) from Australasia.|journal=Mycosphere | url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/00275514.2024.2363211 |access-date=12 September 2024}}</ref>

After joining the [[Tasmanian Field Naturalists Club]] in the 1990s,<ref name=THRoW /> and in recognition of many years of continuous service to the organisation, Gates was subsequently awarded a lifetime membership to the club in March 2021.<ref name=Lifetime>{{cite web
	| url = https://www.tasfieldnats.org.au/archives/past-agm-reports/
	| title = Secretary's Report presented at AGM 4th. March 2021
	| website = Tasmanian Field Naturalists Club Inc.
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
    |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230616213014/https://tasfieldnats.org.au/archives/past-agm-reports/
    |archive-date= 16 June 2023
}}</ref>
Gates was also awarded the Australian Natural History Medallion by the [[Field Naturalists Club of Victoria]] in 2022.<ref name=ANHM>{{cite web
	| url = https://www.tasfieldnats.org.au/news/
	| title = Genevieve Gates Awarded ANHC Medallion
	| website = Tasmanian Field Naturalists Club Inc.
	| date = 6 December 2022
	| access-date = 12 January 2024
    |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230130023903/https://www.tasfieldnats.org.au/news/
    |archive-date= 30 January 2023
}}</ref> In 2023, she was inducted into the [[Tasmanian Honour Roll of Women]] for service to education and training, the environment, and science and research.<ref name=THRoW />
